cards.front: Recall a key point about Art Craft and Design Making Connections
cards.back: Art explores ideas and personal expression; craft emphasises making, skill and material knowledge; design responds to needs, briefs and function.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Art Craft and Design Making Connections
cards.back: The Art, Craft and Design title requires working in at least TWO different disciplines — this breadth is a STRENGTH, not a complication.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Art Craft and Design Making Connections
cards.back: Cross-disciplinary approaches create richer work: painting informed by textile techniques; photography combined with printmaking; 3D design with graphic communication.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Art Craft and Design Making Connections
cards.back: Your portfolio must show both BREADTH (multiple disciplines) and DEPTH (sustained development in each area), connected by a coherent theme.

cards.front: What should you know about art, craft and design exam tips?
cards.back: Show SUSTAINED development in EACH discipline, not just one-off experiments. Explain CONNECTIONS between disciplines — how does your painting inform your photography, or your textile work influence your graphics? Create a COHERENT narrative across your portfolio.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: The Art, Craft and Design title is easier because you can do a bit of everything without going deep. Correct: The Art, Craft and Design title requires you to show both BREADTH across disciplines AND DEPTH within each — it is not a shortcut. cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Art Craft and Design Making Connections
